decks.title: Ohtani’s Dodgers contract
decks.subtitle: An opportunity case for agency leadership

slides.title: Agency leadership | Ohtani's Dodgers contract
slides.kicker: Agency leadership | USD | Evidence cutoff October 13, 2026
slides.subtitle: Exceptional output. A commercial opportunity to value.
bullets: Assess the Dodgers salary commitment against an alternative roster.
Combine baseball contribution with attributable club commercial contribution.
Evidence cutoff: October 13, 2026. Original-decision DCF: December 31, 2023.
slides.notes: Ivory background, navy type, muted gold accent; ample space; direct copy; no personnel humor.

slides.title: Performance earns the first slide
slides.kicker: Agency leadership | USD | Evidence cutoff October 13, 2026
slides.subtitle: The baseball case has measurable substance.
bullets: 2024 regular season: 54 home runs, 59 steals, 1.036 OPS.
2025 regular season: 55 home runs, 1.014 OPS; 47 pitching innings.
Unanimous NL MVP in 2024 and 2025.
Output supports the sporting case; it does not calculate club profit.

slides.title: Commercial evidence | name the recipient
slides.kicker: Agency leadership | USD | Evidence cutoff October 13, 2026
slides.subtitle: Documented club partnerships expand the opportunity.
bullets: ANA announced a multiyear Dodgers partnership in April 2024.
UNIQLO announced a Dodgers partnership in March 2026.
The announcements establish agreements, not fees or sole Ohtani causation.
Player agreements and club agreements have different recipients.

slides.title: Demand indicators | keep their limits
slides.kicker: Agency leadership | USD | Evidence cutoff October 13, 2026
slides.subtitle: Attention is evidence to investigate.
bullets: Ohtani led MLBShop.com Nike jersey sales in the reported 2024 period.
No purchaser geography, dollar proceeds or retained profit was disclosed.
Forbes estimated $125m worldwide off-field earnings for May 2025 to May 2026.
That estimate belongs to the athlete and is not U.S.-only or Dodgers income.

slides.title: Contract | three different measures
slides.kicker: Agency leadership | USD | Evidence cutoff October 13, 2026
slides.subtitle: $700m is the nominal player commitment.
bullets: Reported player payments: $2m annually in 2024–33; $68m annually in 2034–43. USD.
Reported CBT payroll charge: approximately $46m annually. Funding reserves and CBT cash tax are separate.
slides.notes: Reported player-payment schedule. Does not show funding reserves or CBT tax. Full explanatory copy: Reported player payments: $2m annually in 2024–33. Reported deferred payments: $68m annually in 2034–43. Reported CBT payroll charge: approximately $46m annually. CBT payroll charge is a separate measure from the club's cash tax bill.

slides.title: Original-decision model | show the date
slides.kicker: Agency leadership | USD | Evidence cutoff October 13, 2026
slides.subtitle: Payment PV depends on the assumed discount rate.
bullets: December 31, 2023 illustration: nominal pretax USD, year-end payments; discount rates are assumptions.
Salary-payment model excludes CBT cash tax, funding liquidity and other club costs; not today's liability.
slides.notes: Original-decision illustration dated December 31, 2023. Assumed rates; not club cost-of-capital estimates. Full explanatory copy: December 31, 2023 modeled payment PV: $448.7m at 3%, $337.8m at 5%, $256.8m at 7%. Nominal pretax USD; all modeled payments occur at year end. The 5% salary-only annual equivalent over ten years is $43.75m. This is an illustrative DCF, not today's liability or the CBT calculation.

slides.title: Deferral | cash timing needs a second view
slides.kicker: Agency leadership | USD | Evidence cutoff October 13, 2026
slides.subtitle: A $2m player payment is not the full annual burden.
bullets: CBA funding rules require present-value funding by the second July 1 after the earning season.
Actual reserve balances and funding records were not obtained.
Reserve allocations and later player payments must not become two compensation costs.
Model liquidity separately from the player-payment DCF.

slides.title: Club sensitivity | assumptions drive the answer
slides.kicker: Agency leadership | USD | Evidence cutoff October 13, 2026
slides.subtitle: Receipts must become attributable retained contribution.
bullets: Invented example: $100m annual gross receipts × 50% attribution × 40% retained margin.
Result: $20m annual contribution; $154.4m ten-year PV at 5%.
That is $183.4m below modeled salary-payment PV before other club effects.
This is a sensitivity, not actual receipts, a forecast or a contract verdict.
slides.notes: All inputs hypothetical. Contribution excludes modeled salary and other separately omitted costs.

slides.title: Leadership decision | value the alternative
slides.kicker: Agency leadership | USD | Evidence cutoff October 13, 2026
slides.subtitle: Advance the opportunity case; establish incremental club cash flow.
bullets: Compare attributable retained club contribution and avoided roster costs with compensation, marginal CBT tax and other incremental costs.
Obtain the alternative roster, attributable receipts, margins and funding records.
Count sporting benefits once; keep player endorsements outside club receipts.
Update remaining obligations for today. Current evidence does not prove net breakeven or a best-ever ranking.
slides.notes: Merged investment question and leadership decision. Add attributable retained club contribution and avoided alternative roster costs. Subtract compensation, marginal CBT tax and other incremental club costs. Count monetized sporting benefits once. Keep athlete endorsements outside the club ledger. Specify the alternative roster and its expected costs and contribution. Obtain attributable club receipts, retained margins and funding records. Rebuild remaining obligations for a current valuation. Current evidence supports opportunity, not proven net breakeven or a 'best ever' ranking.

decks.title: Two modes. One standard.
decks.subtitle: A proposed U.S. campaign for fictional Switch Audio

slides.title: U.S. advertiser proposal | Switch Audio
slides.kicker: U.S. advertiser proposal | Subject to clearance
slides.subtitle: Two modes. One standard.
bullets: Proposed campaign for a fictional audio brand.
One product moves between a morning call and an evening workout.
Ohtani's participation is subject to athlete, brand and rights clearance.
Customer relevance and incremental contribution determine whether we scale.
slides.notes: Ivory, navy and one muted gold accent. Product close-ups and paired everyday scenes. Calm, precise copy. No internal personnel humor.

slides.title: U.S. activation | start with something documented
slides.kicker: U.S. advertiser proposal | Subject to clearance
slides.subtitle: Personal partnerships have supported concrete U.S. activity.
bullets: New Balance announced a 2024 Fort Worth pop-up for Ohtani's signature collection.
The pop-up offered access 24 hours before the announced launch.
Topps announced a global card agreement that includes U.S.-based products.
These announcements disclose neither campaign profit nor available audio rights.

slides.title: Commercial scope | avoid a false U.S. number
slides.kicker: U.S. advertiser proposal | Subject to clearance
slides.subtitle: U.S.-only athlete earnings remain unknown.
bullets: Forbes estimated $125m worldwide off-field earnings for May 2025 to May 2026.
The estimate includes multiple commercial revenue types.
Checked releases provide no U.S.-allocated earnings amount.
Worldwide estimates and Japan audiences do not establish U.S. campaign reach.
slides.notes: Different scopes and evidence statuses. Unknown does not mean zero.

slides.title: Buyer and product | test the connection
slides.kicker: U.S. advertiser proposal | Subject to clearance
slides.subtitle: Can one pair earn both everyday jobs?
bullets: Proposed audience: U.S. adults considering audio for work and exercise.
Verify call clarity and secure fit before making product claims.
Test whether viewers understand both uses and remember the brand.
Measure spokesperson credibility separately from celebrity recognition.

slides.title: One film | thirty seconds
slides.kicker: U.S. advertiser proposal | Subject to clearance
slides.subtitle: The product stays in frame when the setting changes.
bullets: 0–10 seconds: an approved morning video-call scene demonstrates the microphone.
10–22 seconds: match cut to an approved workout scene demonstrates fit.
22–30 seconds: product close-up, 'Two modes. One standard,' and one purchase prompt.
Prepare six- and fifteen-second cuts from the same approved shoot.
slides.notes: Proposed execution. No claim of approved athlete participation, product performance or asset rights.

slides.title: Creative test | agree the standard first
slides.kicker: U.S. advertiser proposal | Subject to clearance
slides.subtitle: Recognition is the first question, not the final result.
bullets: Compare product-only, Ohtani-led and another spokesperson's ads.
Use comparable U.S. prospective buyers, exposure and media conditions.
Primary creative measures: product-benefit comprehension and brand recall.
Pre-agree thresholds, sample size and cost limits before reviewing results.

slides.title: Sample budget | explicitly invented
slides.kicker: U.S. advertiser proposal | Subject to clearance
slides.subtitle: A $5m scenario makes the commercial hurdle visible.
bullets: Invented rights fee: $3m for a one-year U.S. campaign.
Invented media, creative and activation cost: $2m.
Total hypothetical campaign cost: $5m.
These are teaching assumptions, not Ohtani's rate, a quote or an approved budget.
slides.callout: Invented teaching scenario. Not a quote, forecast or guaranteed return.

slides.title: Incrementality | contribution pays campaign costs
slides.kicker: U.S. advertiser proposal | Subject to clearance
slides.subtitle: At a 25% margin, the scenario needs $20m extra net sales.
bullets: Invented $5m campaign cost. At 25% contribution margin, breakeven requires $20m incremental U.S. net sales.
Estimate incrementality using a holdout. Subtract variable costs in margin; results are neither forecasts nor guaranteed returns.
slides.callout: Invented $5m total campaign cost. Contribution margins are assumptions.

chart.title: Hypothetical breakeven incremental U.S. net sales

slides.notes: Invented $5m cost scenario. Assumed margins; no forecast or guaranteed return. Full explanatory copy: Breakeven incremental net sales = $5m campaign cost ÷ 25% contribution margin. Subtract product, fulfillment, returns and other variable costs in the margin. Estimate incremental U.S. sales with a randomized holdout or justified geographic comparison. Recorded sales and impressions alone cannot establish campaign return.

slides.title: Launch gates | clear the rights, then earn the scale
slides.kicker: U.S. advertiser proposal | Subject to clearance
slides.subtitle: Approve a test; make launch conditional.
bullets: Verify category, U.S. territory, term, channels and existing exclusivity.
Clear athlete approval, product claims and any club or league assets.
Use audience and contribution evidence to decide spending.
Reconcile repeat purchase, cannibalization and spillover within a defined horizon.
